decisions.question: S20 leaves three compatible follow-ups in contracts other than bus-api@v1: bus-testing@v1 G16 (envelopesOf and payloadsOf throw a TypeError on an envelope published through a widened reference), the 'same writer on every later call' wording of stub in bus-testing@v1 G18 and flutter-binding@v1 G17 (the per-type-argument problem G20 had), and an editorial note in nidana-checks@v1 that still describes the older global-accessor definition. Run three more touch steps now, or route them to the producing nodes' phase planning?

options.label: Three more touch steps now
options.consequence: The contracts read consistently before decomposition, at the cost of three steps, each of which can surface further cross-contract follow-ups, as the last five did.

options.label: Route to the producers' phase planning as amend entries
options.consequence: nidana.runtime's and nidana.flutter's phase plans, and nidana.tooling's, emit amend entries for their own contracts, which reconcile folds in; the touch batch ends at S21; the follow-ups are named in those steps' prompts so none is lost.

decisions.chosen: Route to the producers' phase planning as amend entries
decisions.why: Each item is a producer-side semantic of a contract whose producer has not been planned yet, which is what hsdd-phase-plan's amend entry exists for: 'a guarantee or semantic this plan settled for a contract this node owns'. None blocks a decomposition: the runtime decomposition reads S20's registry notes, and nothing consumes these three wordings before the producer plans. Ending the batch here also stops a pattern in which each touch raised the next. The signal that would change this: a decomposition step that needs one of these settled to draw its children.
